chapters.title: Nightglass Courier
chapters.premise: A courier seeking admission to the upper routes abandons his qualifying delivery when a glass ray attacks a suspended maintenance lift. His tiny one-line pulling skill saves a stranded worker and earns a dangerous address.
chapters.emotional_engine: Aren wants his skill acknowledged by the city above; under pressure he chooses the work worth being known for, then resents the price rather than smiling away his ambition.
chapters.future_engine: Deliveries into erased districts, rival couriers and glass fauna expose who controls the city routes. Progression comes from stronger anchors, load judgment and increasingly bold blade-assisted maneuvers.

style_contract.medium: Thin controlled anime contours, elegant facial planes, angular dark hair, tailored pale jacket against black clothing; luminous glass translucency against layered inhabited navy architecture.
style_contract.retain: The integrated invitation of face, creature, city and night atmosphere; inhabited balconies and quiet cyan windows.
style_contract.avoid: Bodybuilder armor, uniform low-angle full-body shots, wet reflective pavement, citywide speckle and a ray inserted behind every close-up.

cast.name: Aren Vale
cast.visual: Light-skinned adult man, slim athletic build, narrow appealing face, gray eyes, swept midnight hair. Tailored ivory waist-length jacket WITH long sleeves over fitted black high-neck top, black slim trousers, plain boots and one red courier cord. Closer to original full Nightglass elegance; distinct provisional adaptation, not automatic original cast selection.
cast.equipment: One solid silver crescent-edge short sword, black straight hilt, cyan pommel ring; RIGHT hand always. Flat sealed cream dispatch wallet on belt.

cast.name: Sera Voss
cast.visual: Light-skinned square-faced woman, copper chin-length bob, burgundy tailored thighcoat, black trousers and boots. City route inspector, dry wit rather than antagonist.
cast.equipment: Simple black short spear carried upright when present; no use in this pilot.

cast.name: Pell
cast.visual: Light-skinned older man with short gray hair, stubble, mustard maintenance jacket and charcoal trousers, broad work harness.
cast.equipment: Harness attached to lift rail until transfer.

cast.name: Glass ray
cast.visual: Single immense navy translucent glass-wing ray, broad crescent wings, cyan circular sensory lights, narrow central beak, one long tail. Living alien animal; no humanoid face.

chapters.setting: Layered vertical city at blue night. Upper admission gate on RIGHT, maintenance lift below LEFT side of same bridge, thick black metal anchor posts. Warm human windows, distant hanging gardens.
chapters.power_rule: Tension Line: one thin cyan line from the RIGHT sword pommel to ONE visible metal anchor pulls Aren toward that anchor. It cannot push or lift the whole maintenance car. Carrying another adult visibly strains his grounded shoulder/stance.
chapters.subtitle: The Delivery Below
chapters.logline: A courier seeking admission to the upper routes abandons his qualifying delivery when a glass ray attacks a suspended maintenance lift. His tiny one-line pulling skill saves a stranded worker and earns a dangerous address.
chapters.reading_premise: Tonight is Aren Vale’s chance to qualify for the upper courier routes. In a city built over darkness, even a short delivery can ask too much.

chapters.title: Black Petal
chapters.chapter_title: A Voice That Knows Your Name
chapters.premise: Ilyra follows her missing brother’s voice into a condemned glasshouse. Its beautiful predator repeats stolen speech; breaking the rooted bloom frees a trapped caretaker but destroys the comforting illusion she came for.
chapters.emotional_engine: Hunger for reunion versus the courage to demand evidence. Ilyra can fight decisively yet remains vulnerable to one familiar sentence.
chapters.future_engine: A trade in cultivated memories leads through haunted estates and impossible gardens. Each case offers a seductive version of a missing person, while Ilyra seeks what actually happened to her brother.

style_contract.medium: Elegant softly modeled pale faces, fine controlled hair edges, desaturated portrait illustration, translucent broad charcoal petals with selective silver filigree.
style_contract.retain: Intimate beautiful unease and scale contrast between tailored human and floral horror.
style_contract.avoid: Anime conversion, armor clutter, all-over silver threads, dense moss grain, gore and generic haunted-house rubble.

cast.name: Ilyra Sen
cast.visual: Pale adult woman, elegant oval face, gray eyes, smooth chin-length dark brown bob with ivory nape underlayer. Black split-tail coat, high white collar, dark pleated combat trousers, slim boots.
cast.equipment: One silver single-edge saber with open oval black guard in RIGHT hand; silver LEFT forearm guard. Small plain silver clasp at collar.

cast.name: Neris
cast.visual: Light-skinned older female caretaker, long angular nose, gray hair in low knot, plain charcoal dress, faded ivory shawl. Wary and practical.
cast.equipment: Plain iron door key on waist cord; no weapon.

cast.name: Mourning Bloom
cast.visual: Enormous translucent charcoal flower, empty oval center edged with sparse silver thorns, broad dark petals, ONE thick tapering root ending in a single thorn foot. No humanoid mask or hands.
cast.equipment: Heavy petals sweep like broad cutting leaves; root pins a door threshold.

chapters.setting: Abandoned curved-rib glasshouse in pale overcast mist. White entrance at LEFT, small caretaker room with a weight-jammed door at RIGHT; broad matte maroon ground, a few pale fallen petals.
chapters.power_rule: The bloom can replay stolen voices only while its single thick root is planted; it must lift that root to turn its heavy face. Root exposed during a committed petal sweep. Ilyra has ordinary saber skill, no new aura.
chapters.subtitle: A Voice That Knows Your Name
chapters.logline: Ilyra follows her missing brother’s voice into a condemned glasshouse. Its beautiful predator repeats stolen speech; breaking the rooted bloom frees a trapped caretaker but destroys the comforting illusion she came for.
chapters.reading_premise: Ilyra’s missing brother is calling from a condemned glasshouse. She knows that voice. She needs to know why it is here.

chapters.title: Soft Thunder
chapters.premise: Tavi tries to recover a caravan’s stolen signal bell from an enormous wind-breathing ram. A brief disastrous contest reveals that the ram wants relief from the painful clang, not treasure, and Tavi negotiates an unconventional ride.
chapters.emotional_engine: A proud improviser wants to travel on her own terms. She learns what the opponent wants and turns a losing contest into a deal without becoming meek or giving up her ambition.
chapters.future_engine: Tavi and a stubborn ram cross living weather-country, taking absurd jobs to reach the far skyports. Her grounded wind-pulse technique grows through timing, breath and using terrain creatively.

style_contract.medium: Rounded expressive cartoon contours, large eyebrows and elastic mouths, opaque block-painted clouds and warm/cool color masses.
style_contract.retain: Muscular charm, broad orange/coral/turquoise palette, enormous creature personality and generous open sky.
style_contract.avoid: Airbrushed plastic, dense individually shaded wool curls, field speckle, fractured ground and particle storms.

cast.equipment: Rounded red gauntlets: anatomical RIGHT has cream circular pressure plate; anatomical LEFT cream crescent. No initial damage. Turquoise cloth padding strip tied around waist over a cream belt; whole strip can be untied and detached.

cast.name: Mara
cast.visual: Light-skinned stocky female caravan captain, silver braid, ochre poncho, dark trousers, stout boots, small blue neck scarf. Amused pragmatist.
cast.equipment: Plain rope halter and caravan tallybook; no weapon.

cast.name: Gale Ram
cast.visual: Living blue cloud-wool ram twice human height, cream muzzle, orange cheeks, curled blue horns, four stout legs and one cloud tail. Broad grouped wool shapes; no armor.
cast.equipment: Plain brass caravan signal bell approximately human-head height, snagged by its strap on near horn; opening broad enough for bulky gauntlets.

chapters.setting: Cream chalk ridge above green windmill hills; wooden caravan platforms and bright cloth sails to LEFT, broad safe grass hollow to RIGHT. A low wooden fence divides paths, with one wide openable gate.
chapters.power_rule: Stored Breath: Tavi charges one short wind pulse in her RIGHT circular gauntlet only while both boots are braced. Losing grounding dissipates any held charge. Release recoils her backward; she cannot recharge airborne. The LEFT crescent glove is defensive.
chapters.subtitle: No Ticket for Thunder
chapters.logline: Tavi tries to recover a caravan’s stolen signal bell from an enormous wind-breathing ram. A brief disastrous contest reveals that the ram wants relief from the painful clang, not treasure, and Tavi negotiates an unconventional ride.
chapters.reading_premise: Tavi needs a seat on the departing sky-caravan. Its signal bell is hanging from a very large, very uncooperative ram.

chapters.title: Red Current
chapters.premise: Ren enters a brutal bridge trial with borrowed gauntlets and wins access to the upper rings by returning a blade-shark’s own strike. His victory is real. So is the debt the weapon writes into his arm.
chapters.emotional_engine: Brash ambition and rivalry: Ren refuses to remain a spectator and is willing to take a frightening shortcut. Winning validates his nerve while exposing the cost he dismissed.
chapters.future_engine: Each higher arena reveals another lender of force. Ren must master what his gauntlets borrow, who collects it and whether victory can free him instead of binding him deeper. Vexa is a rival with reasons to understand that bargain.

style_contract.medium: Black and white directional pen hatching with bold silhouette blacks, athletic angular faces, red gauntlets and localized red impact accents.
style_contract.retain: Kinetic foreshortening, enormous geometric shark shapes, spiral bridge architecture, drawn muscle planes with selective hatch direction.
style_contract.avoid: Glossy gray CGI muscles, shiny vinyl trousers, omnipresent red auras, tiny floor lines and all-over shark swarms.

cast.equipment: Red armored gauntlets. RIGHT has one broad black central plate that lights red when loaded; LEFT has a plain smooth red back. No initial injury, no initial wrist mark.

cast.name: Vexa Rill
cast.visual: Light-skinned athletic woman, sharp cheekbones, cropped black hair with one white forelock, sleeveless charcoal coat with white collar, black trousers and flat combat boots. Cool competitive gaze.
cast.equipment: Small iron upper-ring entry key on cord; folded spectator permit. She does not fight this pilot.

cast.name: Blade-shark
cast.visual: One giant angular white shark-like aerial predator, black upper fins, dark mouth with large triangular teeth, small red eyes. Bold folded-paper planes and traceable tail/fins, not a collage of many fish.

chapters.setting: Vast looping white concrete bridges above a dark sea. Trial platform at lower ring, high spectator rail beyond. A broad dry circular landing zone, one black boundary stripe, no game HUD.
chapters.power_rule: Borrowed Counter: the RIGHT black-plate gauntlet stores ONE directly blocked physical impact and releases it in ONE punch. It cannot stack charges. The spent arm goes numb and a red debt mark appears around that wrist; the cost is revealed only after the release.
chapters.subtitle: One Hit Owed
chapters.logline: Ren enters a brutal bridge trial with borrowed gauntlets and wins access to the upper rings by returning a blade-shark’s own strike. His victory is real. So is the debt the weapon writes into his arm.
chapters.reading_premise: Clear the trial bridge. Earn the upper-ring key. Ren has borrowed gauntlets that can return a monster’s blow—and has barely read the terms.

chapters.title: Floodline Detective
chapters.premise: A flood investigator is asked to explain why a missing man’s coat returned without him. A brief still-water memory and an impossible dry footprint lead to a canal predator carrying its victim, and a deliberately opened sluice.
chapters.emotional_engine: Corin hides his responsibility behind wit and skepticism. He starts by treating a witness as mistaken, corrects himself when evidence contradicts him, and earns trust by solving the immediate danger.
chapters.future_engine: Each flooded district contains a supernatural crime with a physical tell. Corin follows whoever routes living predators through municipal infrastructure while his own past in the flood authority complicates every case.

style_contract.medium: Strong black brush masses, scraped white edges and controlled grayscale planes, limited hot-magenta institutional lights. Graphic ink narrative with selective rough marks.
style_contract.retain: Adult face character, monumental flood infrastructure, black umbrella-segment creature and dry wit under genuine threat.
style_contract.avoid: Glossy leather everywhere, repetitive white water sparkles, polished wet mirror floor, decorative ink splatter over clues.

cast.name: Corin Vey
cast.visual: Light-skinned adult man, lean strong build, angular tired face, short black hair with gray temple, faint stubble. Off-white long coat over charcoal high-neck shirt and belted black combat trousers; flat black boots.
cast.equipment: One long straight iron ward-pole with a broad simple solid C-shaped head: upper shoulder can prop an upper jaw while lower curve catches lower lip. No moving mechanism. Held in both hands when fighting. Small plain black notebook kept inside coat.

cast.name: Ada Marr
cast.visual: Light-skinned adult woman with short blunt blond hair, blunt expressive face, dark hooded rain cape over gray knit top, pale practical trousers and black boots. Direct, angry sister.
cast.equipment: Her missing brother’s dark work coat folded over one arm.

cast.name: Lio Marr
cast.visual: Light-skinned adult man, short dark hair, narrow face, pale rolled-sleeve work shirt, dark trousers, plain boots. Unconscious when first physically seen, then breathing and shaken.
cast.equipment: Small brass municipal sluice key on a cord at neck.

cast.name: Umbrella eel
cast.visual: One thick black segmented canal creature with overlapping umbrella-like membrane ribs, tapering body and broad hinged pale mouth. Two large readable gripping jaws, no human limbs.
cast.equipment: Its wet body moves through connected water; it cannot propel its full weight across the dry high ledge.

chapters.setting: Monumental concrete floodworks. Dry elevated inspection ledge on LEFT, black canal two meters below RIGHT; one broad spillway gap and a tall locked sluice with a magenta signal panel. Water uses large black/white shape groups.
chapters.power_rule: Stillwater Witness: touching an undisturbed pool with two bare fingertips shows ONE brief visual imprint of the last person it reflected. Any ripple erases the imprint. It does not identify motives or predict events. The creature’s dry-ledge limitation is observed physical behavior, not a second detective power.
chapters.subtitle: The Coat That Walked Home
chapters.logline: A flood investigator is asked to explain why a missing man’s coat returned without him. A brief still-water memory and an impossible dry footprint lead to a canal predator carrying its victim, and a deliberately opened sluice.
chapters.reading_premise: Ada’s brother has vanished into the flood city. His coat came home without him. Corin has a notebook, a ward-pole, and one very worried client.
